intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Peutz-Jeghers syndrome (PJS) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the STK11 gene on chromosome 19p13.3. STK11 mutations have not been found in a proportion of PJS families, and a second locus on chromosome 19q13.4 has been proposed.

checks.explanation: The abstract says PJS is autosomal dominant and is caused by germline STK11 alterations. In this family the defect was a heterozygous deletion of STK11, which fits heterozygous causation.

paragraphs.text: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome is an autosomal dominant disorder characterized by melanocytic macules of the lips, multiple gastrointestinal hamartomatous polyps, and an increased risk for various neoplasms, including gastrointestinal cancer (Jenne et al., 1998). agent.process_note: I read all 75 files in full. They are short: mostly abstracts, and many give only a title. Every claim was checked against the abstract text. I took the causal gene (STK11/LKB1, 19p13.3), heterozygosity and autosomal dominant inheritance from the papers. HGNC reference data gave no MIM number for STK11, so the intro has none. Papers with only a title (Jeghers 1949, Scully 1970, Keller 2002 and others) were cited only for what the title says. Uncited: Kallioniemi 1992 (a CGH method paper), Coen 1991 (title does not mention PJS), Schumacher 2005 (title only, no findings), and other title-only papers with no specific content (Bruwer, Dormandy, Bartholomew, Sheward, Keen, Michalany, Farmer, McKittrick, Dodds, Brigg, Yamada). The 4 missense changes from Mehenni 1998 (K78I, D176N, W308C, L67P) are described in Molecular Genetics but are not listed as allelic variants: the abstract does not say clearly which of them were found in patients. No nucleotide-level notation was given for most variants. Penetrance is reported inconsistently (complete in Amos 1997, incomplete in Mehenni 1997), and the entry describes both.
